## §B.2.237 Program-scale recency bias named and a standing corrective installed (§A.18): the session rhythm structurally ratchets attention toward the newest thread and lets the oldest load-bearing claims sit unexamined; the band-wobble history is the fingerprint; the honest long-view is that the core epistemic situation is roughly unchanged across the whole program despite the volume of recent work — bands deliberately NOT moved (a meta-insight is not band-moving evidence) (June 5, 2026)

Prompted by the directive not to let recency shape interpretation — and specifically not at the session scale but **across the whole history of the program**. The session-scale challenge (don't over-weight this conversation's arc) was already addressable; the program-scale version is sharper and is a genuine structural risk the per-session discipline does not catch.

- **The ratchet.** Every session ends by writing an entry, folding it into the master, and updating the resume marker; the next session resumes from that marker. So the newest thread is always the one named, given a confidence line and follow-up targets, while older results settle into unexamined "background," and each marker pulls the next session back toward the most recent thread. Recent work accretes elaboration; old load-bearing claims go un-re-audited. From the inside this is indistinguishable from genuine prioritization. The boost sector has dominated recent history partly because that is where the work happened to go and each marker pointed back at it — not necessarily because it is the most important open question in absolute terms.

- **The fingerprint is already in the document.** The correctness band has wobbled 25-40% → 32-46% → 33-47% → 34-48% → 33-47% in ±1pp steps that each track whichever audit was most recent; the consistency band has been pinned at 89-93% across the entire history. §A.17 already conceded the load-bearing fact: only the relative *moves* were tracked with care, never the absolute *level*. A number that never moves across dozens of intensive sessions is ambiguous between calibrated and anchored — and the ratchet predicts anchored. The §B.2.183→186 G1-count oscillation (≈29 inflated, then discounted to ≈4-5 effective by the audit-of-audit) is the same swing-with-the-latest-pass signature.

- **Symmetric, not deflationary.** The honest danger cuts both ways. This session's late arc was a sustained skeptical read (base rates, "borrowed," "near-definitional," "argued not derived") — several judgments survive scrutiny, but treating the whole arc as the new baseline would be recency capture by the most recent (skeptical) turn. Equally, §B.2.236's joint-forcing finding (SC→gauge+Cabibbo+generations) was the freshest pleasant surprise and must not become *the* headline on freshness alone — it is one cluster resting on one non-standard interpretive bridge (commutant = gauge group), and it does not retroactively firm up the mass-sector retrodictions or the boost sector. The corrective is therefore NOT "be more skeptical"; it is to rebuild from a recency-invariant anchor in both directions.

- **The standing corrective — §A.18 (installed this entry).** (1) The reference class ("foundational derive-everything programs; decades each; none established") is the recency-invariant anchor, because it is not generated by the program's own activity; when the internal momentum-narrative and the external reference class diverge, the reference class is the less-contaminated reading. (2) Volume is not progress — a history that *feels* like momentum is exactly what the ratchet produces. (3) Periodically rebuild the assessment from the *oldest, least-recently-audited* load-bearing claims (on the §A.9 cadence), since that is where a quiet error survives longest. (4) Do not move the bands on a meta-insight — only on band-moving evidence or a deliberate from-scratch rebuild.

- **The least-recently-audited load-bearing claims (now flagged for re-audit, = NEXT_STEPS #4, methodologically elevated).** SM §6 (the A·B "numerical coincidence (8,6)" hedge — the gauge-coupling derivation), the GR ℏ gap-equation circularity rebuttal (App-C flags it; never adjudicated here), Substratum.md, Main.md. These predate the recent boost/audit work and have sat as settled background; the recency corrective makes re-reading them a methodological priority, not mere completeness. This connects directly to the standing concern that the QM-emergence pillar (Barandes-dependent) and the ℏ relation (near-definitional) were assessed long ago and not recently stress-tested.

- **The honest long-view (the point of the exercise).** Across the whole program, the core epistemic situation is roughly what it was many sessions ago: the parameter-free retrodictions are unverified as genuine-vs-fit, the boost sector is open, there is no external review, and the one live empirical contact (DESI running-vacuum) is currently adverse. The large volume of recent structure — engines built, the foundational audit, the joint-forcing finding — has sharpened the *map* of where value concentrates and where the weak points are, but has not moved the framework toward established correctness, and a from-the-inside sense of momentum is precisely what program-scale recency bias would manufacture. That the bands have not moved this session, or genuinely across many sessions, is consistent with both readings (nothing band-moving has happened / the bands are anchored) — and §A.18 records that ambiguity rather than resolving it by fiat.

**Confidence impact: 0pp — and deliberately so.** This is a methodological entry; moving the bands on the strength of a recency-bias reinterpretation would be the exact anti-pattern §A.18 forbids, in either direction. Consistency 89–93%, correctness 33–47% — UNCHANGED, now with an explicit note (§A.18) that their multi-session stability is ambiguous between calibration and anchoring and is to be resolved only by band-moving evidence or a from-scratch rebuild, not by reinterpretation. Binding constraint remains external (§B.2.213). Deliverable: §A.18 (standing guardrail) + this diagnosis; no physics run, no claim refuted, no band moved.

## §B.2.239 Attempted the θ₀=2/9 normalization integral (NEXT_STEPS #1): the §6.1 validation gate reproduces cleanly (1/α₀=23.25), but the integral is NOT the turn-key check it was framed as — the decisive taste-off-diagonal vertex is exactly the unspecified ingredient, and the $1/d$-vs-$1/(2d)$ open question IS the vertex-normalization question, so the integral as specified is circular; the real work is deriving the vertex, not running the loop (June 5, 2026)

Prompted by "proceed as suggested" on NEXT_STEPS #1 — the θ₀=2/9 normalization integral that §B.2.236 had flagged as the cheapest decisive target. Disciplined approach per the standing guardrails and §A.18: read the primary source (SM.md §7.2 spec, §6.1 machinery, §7.1 Cabibbo, §4.7 taste structure) rather than the journal summary, and validate the machinery before trusting any analogous computation.

- **Validation gate PASSED.** Reproduced the §6.1 induced-coupling integral numerically: $\Pi_s(0)=\langle \cos^2 q_\mu/D - \cos^2 q_\mu \sin^2 q_\mu/D^2\rangle_{\rm BZ}$, $D=\sum_{\nu=1}^4\sin^2 q_\nu+m^2$, spatial average $\mu\in\{1,2,3\}$, → $\Pi_s\to 0.3084$ on the plateau $m\in[0.001,0.05]$, giving $1/\alpha_0=6\cdot0.3084\cdot4\pi=23.25$ (I get 23.19–23.34 across grids $N=24$–$48$). The §6.1 measure, the hybrid 4D-loop/3D-vertex structure, and the normalization are confirmed and reusable.

- **The obstruction (structural, not effort).** To evaluate $\mathcal{N}=\lim_{m\to0}\Sigma^{(2)}_{T_1,{\rm off\text{-}diag}}(0)/(g\sqrt{C_2})^2$ I need the explicit taste-off-diagonal *vertex* on the $T_1$ corners — the momentum-dependent factor analogous to §6.1's $\cos q_\mu$. The manuscript supplies the propagator (explicit), the group theory (corners $X_j=\pi e_j$, $C_2(T_1)=2$ — explicit), and points at §6.1's machinery, but never writes the taste vertex factor. §6.1's validated vertex is *gauge-current*, not taste. The Cabibbo derivation (§7.1) — the only other taste-mixing calculation — deliberately bypasses the lattice loop, using the continuum observer propagator $1/|X_j-X_i|=1/(\pi\sqrt2)$ at fixed momentum, so it provides no vertex template. The code repo (`papers/oi_lattice_code/`) is entirely gauge-sector; no taste vertex exists in it.

- **The circularity (the decisive point).** SM.md §7.2 itself (line 818) states the open question as the **$1/d$ vs $1/(2d)$ amplitude normalization**, committed to $1/d$ "argued rather than proved from the Yukawa structure." But $\mathcal{N}=1/d^2=1/9$ vs $1/(2d)^2=1/36$ *is* exactly that factor of four. The integral's value is therefore fixed by the taste-vertex normalization, which is the very thing in question. Writing a vertex that yields $1/9$ would be assuming the conclusion — the invent-the-map / mechanism-shop anti-pattern the standing guardrails forbid. As specified, the integral cannot settle the question it was posed to settle.

- **What it actually means.** The integral is well-posed only *after* the OI staggered Yukawa action and its induced second-order taste-mixing vertex are written out from first principles — and that derivation involves operator/convention choices the manuscript leaves open (which cubic-symmetric Yukawa operator/taste-bilinear; the single-axis-bandwidth $d=\pi$ vs full $2d=2\pi$ momentum convention), at least one of which is the answer. The real work is *deriving the vertex*; the loop integral is the easy part. So θ₀ is not the "cheap, same-class-as-§6.1, in-session-tractable" item it was billed as.

- **Scope correction.** This corrects the framing of NEXT_STEPS #1 and the §B.2.236 characterization ("cheapest, decisive, in-session-tractable with existing machinery, highest leverage"). A clean instance of §A.18 in action: re-auditing a freshly-surfaced target against the primary source caught recency-driven optimism. What held: the validated §6.1 gate is genuinely in-hand and reusable. What did not: the decisive ingredient is the unwritten taste vertex, not a turn-key reuse of §6.1.

**Confidence impact: 0pp.** This does NOT refute θ₀=2/9 — the group-theoretic content (the invariant is $C_2(T_1)=2$; eigenvalue shift ∼ amplitude²; bandwidth normalization a power of $d$) remains forced per §7.2; only the *magnitude-normalization closure* is shown to be non-cheap and currently under-determined at the vertex. Consistency 89–93%, correctness 33–47% — UNCHANGED. The decision on whether to attempt the genuine vertex derivation (option 1 — bounded but real work, requiring the vertex to be fixed independently and the admissible cubic-symmetric Yukawa operators surveyed honestly rather than chosen to land on 1/9) is teed up deliberately, not taken. Deliverable: the validated §6.1 reproduction + this scope correction.

Chosen deliberately: the ℏ derivation is a foundational pillar, §B.2.236 explicitly flagged its circularity objection as *unadjudicated*, and it is genuinely cold (unlike SM §6, read this session for θ₀). Read GR.md §3.1, §3.2 (Steps 1–4), §4, §5, and the §3.2/§6.1 non-circularity discussion from primary source. Symmetric discipline enforced: the θ₀ audit just caught an over-claim, which primes expectation of another — manufacturing a problem here to match that recency would itself be the ratchet §A.18 forbids.

**The derivation chain.** (1) Classical horizon temperature: Jacobson $dE=(c^2\kappa/8\pi G)dA$ + classical entropy density $\eta=1/\epsilon^2$ ⟹ $k_BT_{\rm cl}=c^2\epsilon^2\kappa/(8\pi G)$ — contains no ℏ. (2) Dimensional determination (boundary-only dependence, A and κ excluded on observer-universality grounds): $\hbar=\beta\,c^3\epsilon^2/G$. (3) Thermal self-consistency: the emergent QFT on the same horizon is KMS with Euclidean period $2\pi c/\kappa$, giving $T_Q=\hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_B)$; matching $T_{\rm cl}=T_Q$ (κ cancels) fixes $\beta=2\pi/8\pi=1/4$, so $\hbar=c^3\epsilon^2/(4G)$. (4) Rearranged: $\epsilon^2=4\hbar G/c^3=4\ell_p^2$, $\epsilon=2\ell_p$.

**Adjudication of the circularity objection (App-C).** Largely ANSWERED, and honestly. The three inputs are each ℏ-free: the classical $dE$–$dA$ relation (carrying the 8π Einstein prefactor), the classical counting $\eta=1/\epsilon^2$ (free length ε), and the quantum KMS period (carrying the 2π Euclidean-regularity factor; ℏ enters only on converting period→temperature). Producing ℏ from their matching is therefore not strictly circular, and the 1/4 = 2π/8π is the ratio of an independent quantum-thermal input to an independent classical-gravitational one — genuine, not inserted by hand. It is the same 1/4 as Bekenstein–Hawking, and §5 derives the BH coefficient from the identical matching.

**The honest limitation (conceded in-body).** The gap equation fixes only the ℏ–ε *relationship*, not the *value* of ℏ: §3.2 states "ε is the free geometric input, ℏ is the output," and §4 states the ε=2ℓ_P result "is algebraically equivalent to the formula for ℏ … not an independent determination" — i.e. $\ell_p^2\equiv\hbar G/c^3$ rearranged. So "ℏ derived" must be read as "the functional form + the 1/4 coefficient are derived," never "the value of ℏ is predicted from nothing," a claim the manuscript correctly does NOT make. The predictive content is the specific functional form (it forces the BH 1/4, the CC dissolution, and the Type II RVM form; any other ℏ(ε) fails at least one), analogous to deriving the Schwarzschild metric with M free.

**Lineage, not novelty of ingredients.** This is the Jacobson/Padmanabhan thermodynamic-gravity construction with inputs and outputs swapped (the manuscript says so, §3.2: "the roles of input and output are reversed"; Jacobson assumes {S with ℏ, T with ℏ} ⟹ Einstein 8π, here {Einstein 8π, classical η} + {KMS 2π} ⟹ {ℏ, BH 1/4}). The novelty is the direction. It is explicitly a Tier-1 universality-class result — "not 'OI predicts ℏ uniquely' but 'any horizon-bounded embedded-observer system gets this ℏ'" (§1) — confirming §B.2.236's placement of the ℏ/CC pillar in the borrowed/lineage column rather than overturning it.

**The one over-statement flagged.** The ABSTRACT ("fixes the discreteness scale ε=2ℓ_P as the unique simultaneous solution") reads as a stronger claim than §4's honest "not an independent determination." A skim-reader could take ε as independently pinned; the body corrects this. Minor abstract-vs-body tension; worth a one-line softening in the abstract if the paper is revised, but no substantive defect.

**Symmetric verdict.** Unlike θ₀ (§B.2.239, where the *journal's* framing over-claimed "cheap turn-key"), here the *manuscript* is appropriately humble and the claim holds up as stated: the audit CONFIRMS the honesty rather than catching an over-claim. This is the §A.18 discipline working in the non-deflationary direction — the correct output of a re-audit is sometimes "this one is fine," and reporting that (rather than forcing symmetry-breaking pessimism to match the previous finding) is itself the guard against the recency ratchet.

**Confidence impact: 0pp.** Adjudicates a previously-open objection (App-C circularity) and finds it answered for the functional form and conceded for the value — neither refutes nor newly confirms a load-bearing quantitative claim (ℏ was already correctly placed as lineage/near-definitional in §B.2.236). Consistency 89–93%, correctness 33–47% — UNCHANGED. Remaining cold §A.18 targets: Main.md (QM-emergence/characterization companion) and Substratum.md (the reconstruction/synthesis paper); SM §6 (A·B) was read this session for θ₀ and is no longer cold. Deliverable: this adjudication.

## §B.2.247 "The combination" (#4, the substratum→lattice-PT bridge) pursued to primary source: the deepest gap (gauge measure, Theme 3) is open for the SAME root cause as θ₀ — the explicit map from substratum matter configs to operational lattice-PT objects is unspecified in two sectors. Diagnosis, not closure; it UNIFIES θ₀ / gauge-measure / AB / D10 / Cond2 into one root-cause class and relocates the leverage to a map-derivation program (June 5, 2026)

Acting on "go for the combination" = the high-value-AND-feasible quadrant: #4 (the shared substratum→lattice-PT vertex/measure bridge), the item that compounds across θ₀/AB-separation/D10/Cond2. Read primary source (SM §3.1 background independence, §4.4 the coupling matrix M + Theorem 5 commutant, §6.5 the Haar-vs-pushforward confinement note, §7.5-note on the dynamical-fermion MC, §4.2 Remark on measure reduction). Discipline enforced throughout: this is the area where "never invent the map and prove things about it" bites hardest, so the goal was to CHARACTERIZE the gap from source, not construct a bridge to close it.

**The two measure-correspondence claims, differentiated by status.**
- **(A) Matter/pseudofermion measure** (SM §4.2 Remark; §7.5 gap (i)): substratum real-scalar measure ≈ Berezin pseudofermion measure. Claimed *Level-2 closed* via a Gaussian-covariance match — both bosonic Gaussian, covariances differ by the factor 4 from Theorem 2 ($D_{st}^2=-\tfrac14\Box_{lat}$), absorbable into normalization — modulo (i) sphere-Gaussian projection (classical, large L) and (ii) cycle ergodicity. Pure linear lattice dynamics is INTEGRABLE (frequencies $2\sin(|k|/2)$ not ℚ-independent ⇒ sub-torus, not full shell); "way out (i)" (rounding-induced nonlinearity → chaos) is claimed empirically demonstrated via a measured Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_{\max}=0.0092\pm0.0001$/timestep; analytic derivation of $\lambda_{\max}$ and the $N_{\rm levels}$-independence is open (would elevate to Level 2(a)).
- **(B) Gauge measure** (SM §6.5, §7.5-note): the operational **Haar-HMC** measure vs the framework's claimed **$(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$-pushforward**. The §7.5 mass inputs ($\Sigma\approx0.20$, $m_{\rm match}=0.1234$) are extracted with *standard Haar + Berezin* at weak coupling $\beta\in\{11.1,7.4,3.7\}$. The manuscript states plainly: "whether these standard-measure observables agree with the corresponding observables in the framework's induced $(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$-pushforward measure is open work," with only a leading-order plausibility ("both concentrate near identity": Haar via $\beta\gg1$, $U\approx I+O(1/\sqrt\beta)$; pushforward via $q\gg1$, fraction of non-trivial links $\sim1/q$, $\beta_{\rm eff}\sim\ln q$) and explicitly uncharacterized $O(1/\beta)$ vs $O(1/q)$ corrections. This is the catalog's Theme-3 "possibly the deepest gap."

**The decisive structural finding.** (B) cannot be tested in-session because the object needed to sample the pushforward — the explicit map $\phi\mapsto M(\mathbf{n},\hat e_j)\in SU(N)$ — is **not specified**. §4.4 fixes a single *global* $M\in\mathrm{Mat}(K)$ ("the sole free parameter"), whose commutant gives the gauge *group* (Theorem 5, solid). The gauge *field* $M(\mathbf{n},\hat e_j)$ "determined by $\phi$" is the state-dependent/local promotion (§3.1), but the only "explicit construction" given is the 1D ring toy ($R(i,x)=i{+}2$ if $x_{i+1}{=}0$ else $i{+}1$); the $d=3$, SU(N) link map is asserted, never written. **The theorem.** "Among all second-order reversible nearest-neighbor dynamics on a d-dim lattice of alphabet q, (i) center-independence, (ii) spatial isotropy, (iii) linearity uniquely select the discrete wave equation." Proof: update x_i(t+1)=(f(neighbors)−x_i(t−1)) mod q; CI removes x_i(t)-dependence; isotropy ⇒ symmetric in the 2d neighbors; linearity ⇒ f=α·Σ; α=1 by max lattice speed. Massless lattice Klein–Gordon (Theorem 1: CI ⇔ vanishing mass term).

**Stronger than a skeptic expects (credit).** The three criteria are NOT arbitrary — each is tied to a load-bearing consequence: (a) center-independence is justified by a concrete information-screening argument — if the update contained x_i(t), conditioning on the visible present would determine the hidden state and the process would be Markov ⇒ no P-indivisibility ⇒ no QM; so CI is *the same condition* that yields QM. (b) isotropy ↔ Lorentz. (c) linearity ↔ four convergent arguments (q-gauge invariance, max speed, P-indivisibility maximization, KMS/Unruh thermality for the GR chain).

**The soft spots (the audit's actual finding).**
1. The headline "uniquely selected by CI + isotropy + linearity" silently absorbs three more qualifiers — *second-order, reversible, nearest-neighbor*. Triage: reversibility is clean (from the bijection); range-1/nearest-neighbor is justified by the area-law requirement (routes through GR) and is STRONGER than the stated bounded-degree axiom A3 (a range-2 dynamics satisfies the three headline criteria and differs); second-order-in-time is a structural choice (the Fredkin/leapfrog reversibility form), not forced by reversibility alone, mainly justified by wanting wave-like dynamics (mildly assuming the conclusion).
2. LINEARITY is the live assumption. SM §4.1 claims it "necessary, not merely selected," but criterion 1 (q-gauge invariance ⇒ linearity) rests on nonlinear dynamics being "generically" q-dependent — a genericity claim, not a proof — and Substratum §98/§102 explicitly concedes "nonlinear alternatives are not ruled out" and linearity is "partly derived." This is an INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY between the two papers on the same assumption's status; a referee reading both will catch it. The defensible position is Substratum's (strongly-motivated-not-proven).

**Consequence for §B.2.264.** The "inputs are leaner / no why-cubic knob" framing is right that cubic is downstream, but the knob was RELOCATED into {linearity, range-1, second-order}, not removed — and linearity is the live one. ## §B.2.266 Attempted to STRENGTHEN the linearity-necessity claim from first principles (rather than demote SM per §B.2.265): pressure-tested, a clean equivalence lemma survives (amplitude-independent fluctuation dispersion ⟺ affine/linear), one leg dropped as circular, and the q-gauge ⇒ amplitude-scale-gauge step isolated as the precise open question deciding conditional-vs-unconditional necessity. Formalization DEFERRED to next session. 0pp (June 5, 2026)

Author preferred to strengthen the papers from first principles instead of conceding SM §4.1's "linearity necessary" wording (§B.2.265 had flagged demoting it to the conservative Substratum wording). Attempted a two-leg necessity argument, then pressure-tested it; the result is genuinely informative — half survives as a real lemma, half is circular, and the gap is now named precisely.

**The candidate lemma (survives — worth having).** For the second-order nearest-neighbor reversible rule φ(n,t+1)=F(neighbors)−φ(n,t−1), the dispersion of small fluctuations around a background φ̄ is governed entirely by the Jacobian of F at φ̄. Demanding the dispersion be INDEPENDENT OF THE BACKGROUND AMPLITUDE φ̄ forces the Jacobian to be constant in φ̄ ⇒ F affine ⇒ linear (the additive constant fixed by center-independence/masslessness). Converse immediate. Discrete statement over ℤ/qℤ: all first finite-differences base-point-independent ⟺ affine. So:
  **amplitude-independent fluctuation dispersion ⟺ affine (linear) dynamics.**
This is an equivalence, not a genericity claim — a real upgrade over "x² mod 3 vs x² mod 5 differ, so nonlinearity is generically q-dependent."

**Robustness (why it doesn't collapse to the earlier φ⁴ worry).** φ⁴ has fixed dispersion only around φ=0; around φ̄≠0 its effective mass is m²+λφ̄² — amplitude-dependent — so the lemma correctly flags φ⁴ as nonlinear. A nonlinear relabeling of a linear rule likewise has background-dependent dispersion in its own field variable, so it too is flagged nonlinear. The lemma keys on a physical observable (fluctuation dispersion), which is what makes it stable against these.

**Correction 1 — drop leg 2 (it was circular).** The proposed second leg ("the §4.7 gauge derivation needs a linear coupling matrix, so nonlinearity ⇒ no SM") makes linearity a PRESUPPOSITION OF THE DERIVATION METHOD (linearize → take the commutant of the coupling matrix), not a derived necessity — so using it to prove linearity is circular. Keep it as motivation ("why linearity matters"), discard it as proof. It actually supports the conservative reading.

**Correction 2 — the real gap (the q-gauge link is loose).** The lemma needs AMPLITUDE-SCALE gauge (the field-VALUE scale carries no physics). The framework's stated §2.7 principle is Q-GAUGE (the alphabet SIZE is unphysical). These are cousins, not identical: q-independence of predictions does not obviously entail invariance under rescaling the field at fixed q. The naive repair ("ℤ/qℤ labels are arbitrary ⇒ any relabeling is a symmetry") OVERSHOOTS — relabelings are permutations, and a nonlinear permutation-conjugate of a linear rule would then count as "same physics," which fails to single out linearity at all.

**Honest reconciliation (pending the open step) — both papers should adopt:** linearity ⟺ amplitude-independent dispersion (the lemma); linearity is therefore NECESSARY GIVEN an amplitude-scale gauge principle; whether the framework's q-gauge ENTAILS amplitude-scale gauge is an identified open step. This replaces "generically" with an equivalence lemma and isolates the EXACT missing axiom — a concrete thing to prove rather than a hand-wave. Strengthening, not blind concession. (Refines the §B.2.265 "demote SM" flag: do NOT demote blindly; the reconciliation direction depends on resolving the open step.)

**Status: candidate lemma, NOT proven or inserted.** Deferred to next session.

**Confidence: 0pp.** Attempted analysis + a candidate lemma awaiting adversarial check and one resolved axiom; nothing proven, nothing added to the framework's claims. Bands unchanged (89–93% / 33–47%). A plan/scaffold is 0pp (§A.20); the stopping point is the handoff.

Answering the user's referee-grade question (is amplitude-scale gauge a genuine primitive or does grounding the gauge group on it beg the linearity it implies?) and propagating the resolution.

**The resolution (the substance).** Genuine primitive, NOT viciously circular — but only in the OPERATIONAL formulation, and the distinction is load-bearing:
- STRUCTURAL formulation ("the gauge group is the alphabet's additive-automorphism group") is exposed to the circularity charge. A filesystem check of Main confirmed the QM-emergence uses φ as a bare permutation + trace-out channel and does NOT independently require the alphabet's additive structure (the "linearity" in Main is channel-linearity of Φ, built into QM, not substratum-dynamics additivity). So privileging "+, not the bare set, not the ring" is not forced upstream of the dynamics → structural framing risks assuming linearity to fix the gauge group that yields linearity.
- OPERATIONAL formulation ("absolute field-value scale is unobservable; observer sees only emergent transition probabilities / coupling structure") escapes it: the input is strictly weaker than the output (a nonlinear F on the same alphabet is coherent and is EXCLUDED, not presupposed — the principle has content), and it is the discrete analogue of QFT field-normalization redundancy. It is grounded in §2.7's existing observer-architecture commitment.

**The sharp downstream result (resists the over-claim).** The tempting inference "operational ⟹ linearity is derived, not assumed ⟹ unconditional branch reopens" is FALSE. Deriving "absolute amplitude is unobservable" from the observer architecture is circular because what the embedded observer can resolve is dynamics-dependent: a nonlinear F induces amplitude-dependent emergent dispersion, which IS observable, so "amplitude unobservable" already presupposes linearity. ⟹ Linearity stays CONDITIONAL on an adjoined operational posit. The operational reframing makes the assumption cleaner/better-motivated (and unifies it with 𝒢_sub's generators under the observational-indistinguishability master principle — a real conceptual tightening), but does NOT eliminate it.

"why second-order": different axis — untouched. A·B 48-vs-46.4 coupling tension + offline confinement/mass runs (NEXT_STEPS §0): interacting/measure sector — untouched by amplitude-scale gauge. **Step 1 — relocate the smearing source (clean logical result).** Operator smearing is intrinsically UV-filtering on the modes that run in loops (the visible modes). The faithful (worldline) trace-out of §B.2.261 is an exact change of variables that yields a lattice-faithful visible effective propagator M_eff(k,ω) retaining the FULL visible Brillouin zone — including the cubic-anisotropic structure at the zone boundary. **Step 2 — the boost-sector crux (verified numerically).** Marginal boost LV = a difference between the time and space wavefunction renormalizations, Z_t − Z_s ∝ ∫ K(q)(q_0²−q_x²)/(q²+m²)⁴ d⁴q. Analytically: for a covariant kernel K(q²) the integrand is odd under q_0↔q_x so the integral is exactly 0 (no marginal LV); for a kernel that filters time and space at different scales it is nonzero. MC check (4D, m=1): covariant kernel → Z_t−Z_s = −0.003 ± 0.009 (consistent with 0); anisotropic kernel (Λ_t=1.3, Λ_s=2.6) → −0.374 ± 0.009 (~40σ). **Step 3 — the risk (honest, cautionary).** The framework's natural source of UV filtering is C2 (the hidden sector is SLOW) → a separation of TIMESCALES → a TIME-direction filter. By Step 2 a time-only (or time/space-mismatched) filter is precisely what GENERATES marginal boost LV. So the very mechanism that produces emergent QM (timescale separation) is prima facie boost-ASYMMETRIC. For the coarse-graining to protect the boost sector, its spatial extent must be locked to its temporal extent by the emergent c (a causal-diamond kernel), not a fixed-time-slice average. Whether the OI observer's coarse-graining is causal-diamond-shaped (boost-covariant) or time-sliced (boost-violating) is THE open question — now made precise.

**What would settle it.** Specify the particle-organization map's kernel and check whether it is a function of the emergent invariant interval (causal/boost-covariant — protects) or factorizes into independent time/space filters (boost-violating — fails). This is a MODELING task (the framework must specify the map), not a calculation from current inputs; and the prima facie expectation from C2 is the unfavorable (time-asymmetric) case unless causality is explicitly imposed on the coarse-graining region.

## §B.2.277 Worked the decisive boost question — is the §4.7.1.1 coarse-graining causal-diamond (boost-protecting) or time-sliced (boost-violating)? Honest verdict: the framework does not pin it down (the manuscript says the map's UV-filtering is "not yet characterized"), but the structural pressure is toward TIME-SLICED / boost-violating, and the favorable causal-diamond reading requires structure C1–C3 do not supply. This is an UNFAVORABLE finding — the most pointed structural challenge to the emergent-Lorentz claim so far. 0pp, bands unchanged (boost horn already priced open) (June 7, 2026)

The radiative-LV protection must come from the lossy particle-organization map (§B.2.274), and boost protection (vs merely rotational) requires its kernel to be Lorentz/O(4)-covariant — a causal diamond, not a fixed-time spatial average (§B.2.274 toy: covariant kernel → Z_t−Z_s=0; time/space-mismatched → ~40σ marginal boost-LV). Which is it?

**The argument that it leans time-sliced.**
1. *Protective scale is intrinsically temporal.* A smearing protects only if it filters modes over a region LARGER than one lattice cell (else it is the bare lattice cutoff = unprotected, Collins et al.). The only super-cell scale the framework supplies is the C2 hidden-sector relaxation time τ_hidden (the observer's temporal resolution = how slowly the traced-out bath evolves). That is a TIME scale.
2. *The substrate is 3+1, not 4D-Euclidean-symmetric.* The standard "smearing restores Lorentz at all orders" result lives on a 4D Euclidean (hypercubic) lattice, where a ball-shaped smear is automatically O(4)-symmetric ⇒ boost-covariant after Wick rotation. OI's substratum is cubic-SPACE × distinguished real TIME (the update/evolution direction); it lacks the time–space symmetry that makes Euclidean smearing boost-covariant, so OI cannot inherit the standard protection — its smear must be made covariant by hand against a substrate that already distinguishes time.
3. *The actual coarse-graining is "tall in time, narrow in space."* The temporal extent of the observer's coarse-graining is ~ τ_hidden (large, by C2: slow bath needed for clean QM), while its spatial extent is ~ the emergent particle size (Compton/de Broglie / correlation length), an INDEPENDENT and generally smaller scale. So N_t ≫ N_s ⇒ anisotropic kernel ⇒ time-sliced ⇒ marginal boost-LV by §B.2.274, and not Planck-small (the C2 separation is large by construction).
4. *No c-lock from C1–C3.* For a causal diamond one needs N_s = c·N_t. C1–C3 force N_t large (C2) but impose no matching spatial requirement; the lock is not derivable from the emergent-QM conditions.

**The escape route, fairly stated.** The BARE lattice does have a causal cone (the leapfrog update has finite propagation speed c=1/√3 in lattice units) — a structural, non-dynamics-dependent fact. A coarse-graining defined to fill a bare-lattice causal diamond (N spatial cells, N/c time-steps) WOULD be boost-covariant, non-circularly. So a causal-diamond smear is AVAILABLE in principle. But the framework's actual coarse-graining is driven by C2 (τ_hidden), not by the bare cone, and τ_hidden does not coincide with (particle size)/c — so the available causal diamond is not the one C1–C3 produce. Grounding the lock on the EMERGENT c instead (rather than the bare cone) re-introduces the §B.2.272 circularity (using the c that boost-invariance needs to argue the smear protects c).

**The deeper tension (the real finding).** The SAME condition that produces emergent QM — C2, a slow/high-capacity hidden sector, requiring a large timescale separation — is what makes the coarse-graining time-asymmetric (tall in time). So emergent QM (via C2) and emergent boost-invariance are in structural tension at the level of the coarse-graining geometry: the more cleanly QM emerges (larger C2 separation), the more time-asymmetric the smear, the worse the boost-LV. This is the sharp form of the §B.2.274 "C2 is prima facie boost-asymmetric" observation.

**What would flip the verdict to favorable.** A non-circular demonstration that the observer's particle-organization is intrinsically light-cone-bounded at the BARE lattice level (a causal diamond locked by the bare cone, with N_s = N_t/c·(bare)), rather than set by the C2 relaxation time. The burden is on supplying that; the natural C2-driven reading is unfavorable.

**[CORRECTED in §B.2.278: this entry OVERSTATED the unfavorable case. C2 is a timescale RATIO (τ_S≪τ_B), which is boost-INVARIANT (both dilate by γ) — it does NOT pick a preferred frame as claimed below. And in a relativistic lattice 'slow' = long-wavelength, so the bath's correlations are c-locked (ξ≈c·τ_B) at the BARE level ⇒ a smear tracking bath correlations is a bare causal diamond (boost-covariant, non-circular). So the verdict is NOT 'leans time-sliced' but 'genuinely open with a credible favorable route'; the real residual is boosted-observer equivalence of the QM-emergence with a lattice-rest-frame bath.]** **Status / discipline.** 0pp. This is internal structural analysis (no external verification, no proof of inconsistency — the framework can still posit a causal coarse-graining), so it does not move bands; the boost horn was already priced open. But it is honestly UNFAVORABLE: it argues the framework currently sits on the boost-violating side of the §B.2.274 dichotomy, that the worst-case effect is gross (not Planck-suppressed), and that the fix needs structure C1–C3 do not give. **The asymmetry (well-grounded).** QM-emergence runs through the embedded observer's trace-out (C1–C3, C2 timescale, coarse-graining) — observer-relative. GR-emergence runs through Jacobson thermodynamics, whose four inputs are, per [SM §125]: (i) area law S=η|∂V| — lattice-exact, "no Lorentz invariance enters"; (ii) Unruh T via Bisognano-Wichmann — uses the relativistic dispersion, robust with O(ε²κ²/c²) corrections; (iii) Clausius δQ=∫T_μν — "no Lorentz invariance required," exact; (iv) Raychaudhuri — kinematic, exact. So 3 of 4 inputs are Lorentz-independent ⇒ the emergent metric/causal structure is covariant and robust, NOT subject to the C2/coarse-graining boost worry.

**Why it helps (resolves the §B.2.278 crux if it holds).** §B.2.278's open crux was boosted-observer equivalence: does a boosted observer (vs the lattice-rest bath) recover the same emergent c? If matter is referred to the SHARED, robustly-covariant emergent geometry (the GR light cone) rather than to each observer's own C2 partition, all observers agree because they agree on the metric. The geometry becomes the observer-independent backbone; QM is each observer's description referred to it. The §B.2.278 favorable route (causal-diamond smear) would then be supplied BY the GR sector, non-circularly (the metric is fixed by the tree-level/thermodynamic structure, loops act within it). A covariant geometry does NOT automatically make the matter cutoff covariant — only if the §4.7.1.1 matter coarse-graining is referred to the emergent metric's light cone rather than the lattice/C2 scale. That coupling is exactly what the framework leaves uncharacterized. So the insight RELOCATES the open question to "does matter inherit the geometry's causal structure?" — better-founded and more tractable, but unestablished.

4. Circularity guard: works only if the metric/cutoff is fixed by the tree-level/thermodynamic structure, not the loop-corrected dispersion.

**Discipline.** This is a physical-mechanism proposal (legitimate to evaluate), not parameter tuning. **Read of the construction ([Structure]/[SM]).** The coupling graph is combinatorial — connectivity "read off from φ," NO edge weights/lengths ("any spatial embedding is for human convenience, not a physical fact"). Geometry = connectivity's deviation from flat ℤ^d via OR curvature (optimal transport). So the §B.2.280 √w-vs-w ambiguity presupposed weighted edges the framework does not have; it dissolves.

**Tree-level universal coupling (clean, non-circular).** Matter (graph Laplacian L) and geometry (κ_OR) are both functionals of the one graph. **Numeric check (caught an overclaim, sharpened the result).** Anisotropic combinatorial deformation (integer edge multiplicity m_x:m_y). Matter: g_xx/g_yy = (1/m_x)/(1/m_y) exactly (c_i²=m_i). Claim survives, sharpened: shared because matter and OR-Ricci are both governed by the one Laplacian. (Without the check I'd have loosely claimed "transport metric matches" and been wrong about resistance.)

**Caveat.** Holds to the extent the curved coupling graph is in the regime where those convergence theorems apply (random-geometric-graph-like) — the SAME assumption the GR derivation rests on. Conditional on something already assumed, not on anything new.

**Net.** §B.2.279 sub-check (a) affirmative at tree level: matter inherits the geometric light cone, cleanly. Tree level now fully consistent: substratum relativistic + partition-independent (§B.2.281); faithful trace-out preserves c (§B.2.261); matter couples to the shared metric g (this entry). ⇒ The ONLY remaining place for LV is the loop level in the lossy §4.7.1.1 step: does it cut matter loops relative to g, or introduce a frame? C2's observer-independence is consistent with EITHER: a coarse-graining can satisfy an observer-independent slowness condition and still organize by lattice simultaneity rather than the observer's own causal structure.

**Net.** Clearing C2 narrows the problem (removes a candidate culprit + the doomed reading) but does not close it. ## §B.2.286 Escape-route audit (consolidated): five tempting ways to dissolve the boost problem, each examined and found real-but-insufficient or circular — all bottoming out at the same unwritten lossy §4.7.1.1 map. Documented to pre-empt reviewer objections and prevent re-running them. 0pp, bands unchanged (June 7, 2026)

Context: a run of conversational probes each proposed a way the boost/radiative-LV problem might dissolve. Honest verdict on each:

1. **"Maybe relativity is just wrong (approximate LI)."** Real and AVAILABLE for the *small* residual — the framework already takes it for the bare O(k⁴) anisotropy (⟨δ⟩=1/90, Planck-suppressed, allowed). But it does NOT rescue the *gross* failure mode: Leg 3 (§B.2.283) showed a 2:1 kernel mismatch shifts c ~50%, which is excluded by LV bounds (parts in 10²⁰+ across birefringence, GRB dispersion, clock-comparison, cosmic-ray thresholds). "Approximate LI" buys a tiny residual, not a 50% effect. Doesn't reach the problem.

2. **"The LV bounds are seen through observational incompleteness."** Kernel of truth: incompleteness DOES launder *absolute/universal* quantities (absolute field scale, energy zero, overall c-rescaling) — that's the amplitude-scale gauge (§B.2.272) and the CC dissolution, both correct. But the LV bounds are *differential* (polarization vs polarization, energy vs energy, direction vs direction); a universal distortion cancels from them, and dangerous LV is non-universal (direction/energy/species-dependent). Also we sit at ~370 km/s vs the CMB frame, so a lattice-frame tilt is NOT aligned with our rest frame. Limit argument: a lopsidedness that reproduced relativity to 10²⁰ just IS Lorentz invariance operationally (= the success outcome). Lens is gauge on absolutes, physical on differentials; LV-that-matters is differential. Shut.

3. **"Relativity is a projection artifact, like QM."** It's the framework's actual thesis (and the faithful part already hides the frame, §B.2.281). ## §B.2.298 SHARPENING (user: the partition is for OBSERVABILITY, not EXISTENCE). Correct; corrects §B.2.297-era "partition needed for everything." Splits the framework into existence-layer (substrate, partition-free; geometry, CC; preferred frame lives here but is fine/unobservable) vs observability-layer (partition-relative: QM, particles, measured physics; boost gap lives here). **The correction.** Partition = about observability (what a subsystem can access about the rest), NOT existence. Bare substrate configuration just IS — definite, classical, complete, partition-free. QM is what becomes AVAILABLE under a partition, not a condition for matter to exist. §B.2.297-era "partition needed for everything" was imprecise: needed for observable-as-quantum, NOT for existence. Deep-space electron exists as substrate regardless; quantum description is partition-relative.

**Two-layer split (along the user's line).**
- EXISTENCE layer: substrate, partition-free. Geometry/GR, CC dissolution live here. Preferred frame (lattice/stepping) lives here too — but that's FINE (real-but-unobservable, Lorentz-ether-undetectable, §B.2.289; framework explicitly OK with an undetectable preferred frame).
- OBSERVABILITY layer: partition-relative. QM, particle-organization, measured speeds. ONLY place the boost problem can bite.

**Consequence 1 — generalizes the firewall.** Existence layer partition-free ⇒ boost problem CANNOT threaten substrate ontology, geometry, or CC dissolution (existence-layer claims). Boost is at most a threat to EMPIRICAL ADEQUACY (reproducing observed Lorentz invariance in the matter sector), NOT to consistency or the gravitational results. Worst case for boost = takes down the SM-Lorentz claim, not the ontology. (Consistent with CC = Tier-1/substratum-independent, prior result.)

**Consequence 2 — the posit becomes EPISTEMIC.** If the organization map is observability-layer, positing it covariant is a claim about HOW OBSERVATION WORKS (defensible by what an embedded observer can access), NOT a brute ontological stipulation. Epistemic posit ("observers organize this way because that's what access permits") is more benign at review than ontological ("universe fine-tuned this way"). Puts the posit in the right home.

**Honest limit (does NOT dissolve).** The observability layer is BY DEFINITION what gets measured; the boost violation is a measured quantity (species c_eff). "Only observability, not existence" doesn't make it harmless — empirical adequacy REQUIRES the observability layer to come out Lorentz-invariant. The bound and the putative violation are both in the observability layer; calling it epistemic doesn't move it out of experimental range. Existence-partition-free protects the ontology; the framework still must deliver a Lorentz-invariant observability layer = the open gap.

**Net.** "Why need the observer for anything else?" resolved: need the PARTITION only for the observability layer (the bridge to measured physics), NOT for existence (substrate-only). Embedded observer (partition sense) = bridge to WHAT WE MEASURE, not a condition for WHAT IS. Boost problem = a defect in that bridge (empirical-adequacy risk, observability layer), NOT a flaw in the ontology or a whole-framework inconsistency. Most accurate placement reached.

**Confidence: 0pp.** Ontological clarification; corrects prior overstatement, generalizes the firewall, reframes posit as epistemic; does not dissolve the empirical-adequacy gap. Consistency 89–93%, Correctness 33–47% — UNCHANGED.

BUT a shared ceiling ≠ a shared value: species can settle at DIFFERENT high-energy group velocities BELOW the cone, all ≤ c_bare but unequal. The killer is these SUB-ceiling differences (Collins, O(g²/loop)~1% if organization non-covariant); the cone-ceiling caps without forcing equality.

**Observer-dependence is the safe half.** c-as-each-observer's-limit = the (a)-type universal-frame aspect, HANDLED (gauge/partition-relative, §B.2.299). Species-universality = (b)-type DIFFERENTIAL, NOT observer/frame-dependent (differ below the cone in one frame ⇒ differ in all). Observer-dependence applies to the safe part, orthogonal to the open part.

**Framing value + why not automatic.** "c is the cone" correctly makes universality the NATURAL expectation (one causal structure ⇒ one cone ⇒ all on it; species-dependence looks manufactured). But Collins = the demonstration that this default FAILS under quantum corrections without a custodial symmetry, and §B.2.297 = OI has none for the time-space coefficient. So the framing names what we want; Collins names why it isn't free.

**Net.** "c is the cone" earns a shared CEILING + correctly frames universality as natural, but the measured killer is radiative species DIFFERENCES BELOW the ceiling, which the cone doesn't forbid and OI has no symmetry to forbid. Same organization-map gap, most physical form: do all species SATURATE the one cone identically (relativistic) or fall below it by coupling-dependent amounts (LV)?

**Question (§B.2.311 item b).** All §B.2.310/311 boost-LV came from the spatial-only vertex (W=Σ_{i=1}³cos²q_i, "no time-direction gauge connection") — structurally temporal gauge (A_0=0). Is that apparent time-space asymmetry physical LV or a gauge artifact (cancels in gauge-invariant/transverse quantities)?

**Method.** One-loop lattice scalar-QED tensor VP Π_μν(p) (Wilson scalar: G=1/(q̂²+m²), q̂_ν=2sin(q_ν/2); bubble V_μ=2sin(q_μ+p_μ/2); seagull = the CORRECT p-INDEPENDENT tadpole δ_μν Σ_q 2cos(q_μ)G(q), verified analytically via the total-derivative identity Σcos(q_μ)G=2Σsin²(q_μ)G² ⇒ Π_μν(0)=0). Finite-T-style projection: physical transverse Π_T=½(δ_ij−k_ik_j/k²)Π_ij; longitudinal Π_L=(k_ik_j/k²−p_ip_j/p²)Π_ij. LV = (Z_time−Z_space)/avg of the projected scalar, Z's from a joint 2D quadratic fit of the projected Π over (ω,κ). Wilson-scalar (not staggered) is the right tool for the gauge-vs-physical STRUCTURE (it's about temporal gauge, universal); staggered specifics belong to the later OI-coefficient calc. Scripts: obligationA_gauge2.py, obligationA_gauge3.py.

**Ward validation.** Covariant vertex: |p̂·Π|/|Π| = 1e-3–3e-3 (transverse to grid error) ⇒ machinery validated, seagull correct. Spatial-only vertex: residual ~0.1 (NOT 4-transverse) — expected: temporal-gauge structure replaces 4-transversality with the Gauss-law constraint; the failure is in the absent Π_0ν (longitudinal/constraint) sector, not the physical transverse sector.

**Results (robust across n=36/44, m=0.06/0.10).**
- PHYSICAL transverse photon: LV = +0.0016, −0.0007, +0.0038 ⇒ consistent with ZERO (grid-error ±0.004). Covariant at the marginal (dim-4) level.
- LONGITUDINAL sector: LV = +3.09, +3.12, +3.09 ⇒ O(1), robust. The LV lives ENTIRELY here.
- Naive scalar proxy (§B.2.310/311 measure, same grid): −0.055.
- Transverse LV IDENTICAL for spatial-only and covariant vertex (Π_ij block is the same object; the spatial-only restriction only zeroes Π_0ν).

**Interpretation.** The spatial-only-vertex ("no temporal gauge connection") boost-LV is a TEMPORAL-GAUGE ARTIFACT: it sits in the longitudinal/constraint sector (non-propagating), while the physical transverse photon — the propagating gauge-invariant mode — is covariant at dim-4. This is exactly how temporal gauge behaves in ordinary Lorentz-invariant gauge theory. The scalar proxy of §B.2.310/311 was measuring (mostly) the gauge sector. ⇒ the boost-LV worry is substantially REDUCED, not merely relocated: the physical, gauge-invariant marginal boost-LV from this loop is consistent with zero even WITHOUT smearing.

**Combined boost picture now (two independent reductions):** (1) GAUGE-CONFINEMENT (this entry): most apparent marginal boost-LV is longitudinal/gauge, absent from the physical transverse photon. (2) SMEARING-SUPPRESSION (§B.2.311): any residual is suppressed ≥O(a²) by the derived heat-kernel smearing. Together ⇒ the marginal boost-LV is far less threatening than the bare scalar proxy suggested.

**Caveats / still open (NOT inflated).**

(2) Spatial-only tensor not 4-Ward-transverse ⇒ a rigorous OI statement needs the Gauss-law/constraint treatment of the DISCRETE-TIME substrate (continuous-time Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory has this built in; OI's discrete time needs it shown). The physical transverse photon here is well-defined because it equals the covariant theory's Π_ij, but rigor needs the constraint.
(3) Covariant transverse LV≈0 is partly expected (Euclidean lattice 0↔i is a hypercubic symmetry); the nontrivial content is that the spatial-only BREAKING of 0↔i does NOT leak into the transverse sector.
(4) Combining (1)+(2) needs GAUGE-COVARIANT smearing (naive internal-line smear breaks Ward).

# §B.2.415 LITERATURE SEARCH for the V_4g verified reference (residue item 4) → FOUND the canonical anchor (Capitani, Lattice Perturbation Theory, Phys.Rept. 2003, hep-lat/0211036), located the exact sections; this CONVERTS item 4 from "external/unanchored" to "external-anchor-IDENTIFIED, needs conventions-matched transcription" — but does NOT itself resolve the factor-14 (transcription + matching still required, honestly not done from snippets). Owner: search the research literature for the V_4g reference. Searched "Wilson lattice gauge action four-gluon vertex explicit form." RESULTS: the canonical source is Capitani's review (hep-lat/0211036, Phys.Rept. 384 (2003) 71), §5.2 "Pure gauge action" — it derives the gluon vertices by expanding the plaquette U's in the algebra A's via BCH, and the search returned its explicit 3-GLUON vertex Eq. 5.25: W_{μνλ}^{abc}(p,q,r) = -i g0 f^{abc}(2/a){δ_μν sin(a(p-q)_λ/2)cos(a r_μ/2) + cyclic}, p+q+r=0, reducing to the continuum 3-gluon vertex as a→0. The 4-GLUON vertex is in the SAME section (the plaquette expansion generates all n-gluon vertices; the 4-gluon is the next term). Critically for the OI V_4g tadpole: §15.4.4 "Operator tadpole" + §15.4.6 "Quark self-energy (tadpole diagram)" give the worked tadpole-diagram machinery (the seagull/tadpole topology where the 4-gluon or operator-tadpole vertex contracts two legs into a loop) — exactly the structure of the OI V_4g tadpole whose cosine-placement is ambiguous. Capitani §16 (computer codes) + §17-18 (lattice integrals, algebraic 1-loop method) + Appendix A (notation/conventions) give the conventions needed to MATCH. SECONDARY anchors found: Constantinou-Panagopoulos-Skouroupathis (hep-lat/0606001, cactus/tadpole resummation, explicit dressed gluon vertices); the anisotropic-lattice Feynman-rules paper (hep-lat/0303005) noting one-plaquette actions change only the O(a²) terms in the 4-and-higher gluon vertices (relevant: confirms the 4-gluon vertex's leading structure is action-independent, the irrelevant terms are where the cos-placement subtlety lives). WHAT THIS SETTLES vs DOESN'T: SETTLES — the verified reference EXISTS and is IDENTIFIED (Capitani §5.2 for the explicit Wilson 4-gluon vertex; §15.4.4/§15.4.6 for the tadpole-diagram application; conventions in App. A). The two OI derivations (pair-topology vs per-topology, differing by the 2cos(p_μ)Σcos(k_γ) piece, factor ~14) can now be checked against Capitani's explicit vertex + tadpole worked examples. This is the "verified reference vertex" the framework said was needed. DOES NOT SETTLE — I have NOT transcribed Capitani's explicit 4-gluon vertex here (the front-matter fetch returned the TOC/intro, not §5.2 body; and per the §B.2.414 discipline, transcribing a 4-gluon lattice vertex from search snippets and declaring the resolution would be the exact false-positive trap — the cos-placement is precisely the error-prone detail). Resolving the factor-14 requires: (a) fetch/obtain Capitani §5.2 4-gluon vertex Eq. (the next eq. after 5.25) + §15.4.4 tadpole worked example, (b) match conventions (a, g0 normalization, generator normalization Tr[T^aT^b]=½δ^ab, momentum routing) to the OI Π_s scheme, (c) check which OI derivation (pair vs per-topology) reproduces Capitani's cos structure. That is a careful conventions-matched transcription task — now WELL-DEFINED and anchored, but not completed in-session (and not safely completable from snippets). VERDICT: item 4 UPGRADED from "external, no anchor" → "external anchor IDENTIFIED (Capitani §5.2 + §15.4.4), resolution = conventions-matched transcription against it, well-defined but not snippet-safe." The honest next step is to fetch the specific Capitani §5.2/§15.4 pages (arxiv PDF body) and do the matching carefully, OR have a collaborator with the reference do it; either closes item 4. Recall: V_4g is a SUBLEADING systematic — the headline A·B=48±1.5 is independent of it (§660), so this anchors a refinement, not a blocker. NO band/manuscript change (literature search; identified the verified reference + located exact sections; did NOT manufacture the resolution from snippets, per discipline). 0pp. Consistency 89–93%, Correctness 33–47% — UNCHANGED (June 12, 2026)

# §B.2.417 V_4g "over the line" attempt — STRUCTURAL DISCRIMINATOR found + then SELF-CORRECTED: the discriminator sharpens the question to a definite checkable claim but does NOT settle it (the gauge 4-gluon vertex's own loop-cosine structure is exactly the undetermined piece); honest verdict = NOT resolved in-session, narrowed to one explicit equation. Owner: get V_4g over the line. Retrieved (primary source) the lattice TADPOLE structure from THREE independent references: Capitani §15.4.6 Eq 15.128 (fermion tadpole), Capuzzi et al. 1006.2009 Eq 79-80 (minimally-doubled, V2(p,p) "depends only on external momentum", Z0=∫1/p̂²=0.1549..), and the noncommutative-gauge tadpole hep-th/0404038 App C. STRUCTURAL DISCRIMINATOR (genuine, not analogy): the lattice tadpole/seagull I=(1/2)∫d^dk G(k)·V2(p,p) absorbs the LOOP-momentum cosines into the scalar Z0-integral, leaving the surviving vertex factor a function of EXTERNAL momentum p only (e.g. Σ_ρcos(ap_ρ)). The OI factor-14 traces (§660) to a 2cos(p_μ)Σ_γcos(k_γ) piece that MIXES external p and LOOP k — present in per-topology, absent in pair-topology. INITIAL READ: the cross-term looks like a retained loop-cosine that a pure tadpole should have integrated into Z0 → would favor pair-topology. SELF-CORRECTION (the discipline catch, before committing): the gauge 4-GLUON vertex is genuinely MORE complex than the fermion seagull V2 — the 4-gluon vertex DOES carry loop-momentum-dependent cosine factors AT THE VERTEX (unlike the simple fermion V2 which is external-only), and some legitimately survive as part of the loop integrand BEFORE integration. So the 2cos(p_μ)Σ_γcos(k_γ) cross-term might be a REAL feature of the gauge vertex that the PAIR-topology form wrongly DROPPED — which FLIPS the lean vs the §B.2.416 fermion-tadpole hint. ⟹ I CANNOT conclude which form is correct from the discriminator alone: distinguishing "legit gauge-vertex loop-cosine (→ per-topology right)" from "spurious retained cosine (→ pair-topology right)" requires the EXPLICIT Capitani Wilson 4-gluon vertex equation, which I still have not retrieved (the §5.2 body did not surface; searches return the fermion tadpole, the 3-gluon vertex, continuum 4-gluon, and non-perturbative lattice 4-gluon — never the perturbative lattice pure-gauge 4-gluon vertex). HONEST VERDICT: NOT resolved in-session. What the discriminator DID achieve: it converts the vague factor-14 into a SHARP, definite, checkable physical question — "do the loop-momentum cosines in the gauge 4-gluon tadpole vertex belong inside the Z0 loop-integration (pair-topology) or do some survive at the vertex as genuine loop-dependent factors (per-topology)?" — answerable IMMEDIATELY by the one missing equation. The two OI forms make physically definite, mutually-exclusive claims; the reference equation adjudicates cleanly. RESISTED (twice now): I declined to commit to the structural-discriminator lean once I saw it could flip on the gauge-vertex's own loop-cosine content — manufacturing "pair-topology, resolved" from the fermion-tadpole structure would have been the false-positive trap, and I caught it in self-correction before logging a resolution. STATUS of item 4: narrowed from "anchor identified" (§B.2.415) → "method retrieved, weak hint" (§B.2.416) → "question sharpened to a definite yes/no checkable against ONE explicit equation (Capitani Wilson pure-gauge 4-gluon vertex); both OI forms make mutually-exclusive checkable claims; NOT settled without that equation" (§B.2.417). The equation needs a non-truncated §5.2 source (Rothe textbook Ch. has it explicitly; or Capitani PDF body pages; or a collaborator) — bounded, specific, but genuinely not obtainable from the searches run. V_4g remains SUBLEADING (A·B=48±1.5 independent, §660). # §B.2.419 V_4g RESOLVED (structural cos-placement) via the EXPLICIT Wilson 4-gluon vertex (Capitani Eq 5.28 = Rothe 1997, from the owner-uploaded full PDF) → PER-TOPOLOGY form is correct; this FLIPS the §B.2.418 indirect 4-to-1 lean, vindicating the §B.2.417 refusal to commit. Owner uploaded 0211036v2.pdf (full Capitani review, 221pp). Read §5.2 directly (file-reading skill, pdfplumber): retrieved the explicit 4-GLUON vertex Eq 5.28 W^{abcd}_{μνλρ}(p,q,r,s), attributed in-text to "(Rothe, 1997)" — the exact primary source flagged in §B.2.418 download-paths (a)+(c) jointly. STRUCTURE (the decisive feature): the 4-gluon vertex carries cosine factors cos(a(·)_μ/2) whose arguments are DIFFERENCES of the four leg momenta (q-s, k-r, q-r, k-s, ...) and hatted momenta k̂_μ=(2/a)sin(ak_μ/2). On the TADPOLE contraction (two legs → loop k,−k; two → external p,−p), a difference-argument cosine cos(a(q-s)_μ/2) with one loop + one external leg becomes cos(a(p∓k)_μ/2) = cos(ap/2)cos(ak/2)+sin(ap/2)sin(ak/2) → GENUINELY produces EXTERNAL×LOOP cosine cross-terms cos(p_μ)cos(k_γ) at the vertex. DECISIVE: the Wilson 4-gluon vertex DOES carry vertex loop-momentum cosines that mix with external momentum — it is categorically RICHER than the fermion seagull V2 (which was external-momentum-only, hence genuinely factorized into vertex×Z0). So the 2cos(p_μ)Σ_γcos(k_γ) cross-term is a REAL, REQUIRED feature of the correct gauge tadpole, NOT a spurious retained piece. ⟹ the OI PER-TOPOLOGY derivation (which KEEPS the cross-term) is STRUCTURALLY CORRECT; the PAIR-topology derivation (which DROPS it) is MISSING a real piece. RESOLUTION: per-topology. This FLIPS the §B.2.418 indirect "4-to-1 lean toward pair-topology" — the four indirect refs were FERMION tadpoles (V2 external-only, genuinely factorizes) or ASSEMBLED gluon-SE results (cross-terms pre-summed); their external-only structure does NOT carry to the gauge 4-gluon vertex. The §B.2.417 SELF-CORRECTION (warning the lean could flip on the gauge vertex's own loop-cosines, refusing to promote pair-topology) is now VINDICATED by the explicit equation: it DID flip. Holding "strong lean not resolved" at §B.2.418 was correct — committing to pair-topology would have been WRONG. METHODOLOGICAL NOTE: this is the payoff of the whole discipline arc (§B.2.414-418) — refusing to manufacture a resolution from indirect evidence (twice tempted: the fermion-tadpole hint §B.2.416 leaning per-topology, the 4-to-1 indirect lean §B.2.418 leaning pair-topology, OPPOSITE directions) until the actual primary-source equation settled it. The indirect leans pointed BOTH ways; only the explicit vertex was decisive. CONFIDENCE/SCOPE (honest): HIGH confidence on the structural cos-PLACEMENT (per-topology correct) — read directly off the explicit primary-source vertex Eq 5.28, the exact object §660 says the factor-14 traces to. Does NOT by itself recompute the exact A·B shift: §660 brackets it ~3-12%, and per-topology-correct points to the LARGER (upper, ~12%) end. A full recompute = plug Eq 5.28 into the tadpole integral with OI conventions (N_f=6, T(R)=1/2, Π_s normalization) — a finite well-defined task now that the vertex is fixed (could be a future kit). IMPACT on the main result: V_4g is a SUBLEADING systematic; headline A·B=48±1.5 is independent of it (§660). For staggered D (anti-Herm hopping) Tr[D⁻¹]=mass·Tr[(D†D)⁻¹] exactly (odd piece traces to zero), so the two differ by a factor `mass` — this was the ENTIRE ~10× (=1/mass at m=0.1) discrepancy the G1 cross-check threw up. k6 is correct/standard; the standalone kit's normalization is the same physics scaled by mass but nonstandard. G2 induced q→∞→free: reldiff 0.42→0.18→0.058→0.015→0.0015 (q=16..4096), tail-monotone, 0.15% limit, PASS (used exact-dense per config + 24 cfgs to kill estimator noise; same tighten-not-weaken move as §B.2.422). # §B.2.424 V_4g PER-TOPOLOGY SHIFT KIT — built on the existing AB_derivation pipeline (checked first this time). Owner: build the V_4g exact-shift kit. FIRST read the existing machinery (lesson from §B.2.423): papers/oi_lattice_code/gauge/AB_derivation/ has reproduce_AB.py (headline A·B=48±1.5), tadpole_wilson_v4g.py AND v4g_extension.py — both already compute a V_4g tadpole, and tadpole_wilson_v4g.py's OWN header flags the exact open question: "my derivation has uncertainties in the signs and overall factor... cross-check against Capitani 2003 Eq 2.84 pending... overall sign and magnitude provisional." It derived the tadpole from the PAIR-topology assumption → transverse integrand J_pair=<cos(k_μ)/k̂²>→0.0299, a +3.8% A·B shift. So the kit is NOT new-from-scratch: it resolves the pending cross-check this file flags, using the primary source the §660→§419 arc settled on. Extracted Capitani Eq 5.28 (Wilson 4-gluon vertex, attrib. Rothe 1997) from the owner-uploaded PDF (/mnt/user-data/uploads/0211036v2.pdf, p.31-32) — OCR noisy but the STRUCTURE is unambiguous: leading terms are products of TWO difference-argument cosines cos((q−s)_μ/2)cos((p−r)_ν/2) spanning all four legs (NOT one cos per pair). On tadpole contraction (ext ±p, loop ±k) the identity cos((p±k)/2)=cos(p/2)cos(k/2)±sin(p/2)sin(k/2) leaves sin·sin CROSS-TERMS depending on both ext and loop momenta = vertex loop-cosines the pair-approx drops (the §419 finding, now coded). KIT (code/v4g_shift_kit_B2_424/v4g_per_topology.py): computes J_pair and J_per on the same grid + the existing compute_pi_s, with a w_cross switch; GATES V1 (cross-off reproduces existing J=<cos/k̂²>, diff 3e-8 = k=0-mask convention) V2 (J_per finite 1/N² continuum limit 0.0924) V3 (cross-term Δ>0 ∀N) ALL PASS. RESULT — STATED HONESTLY (refused false precision): the cross-term is an EXACT BZ identity Δ=w_cross/8 (independent of N; verified <(1−cos k0)/k̂²>=1/8 via <k̂0²/k̂²>=1/4). ROBUST: existence + SIGN of the cross-term (Δ>0) are fixed by Eq 5.28's difference-argument cosines → per-topology shift strictly LARGER than pair's +3.8% → V_4g systematic at UPPER part of 3–12% bracket (consistent w/ §419). NOT PINNED by this kit: the exact coefficient w_cross hence exact magnitude — sweep shows w_cross 0/0.25/0.5/1.0 → shift +3.8/+7.8/+11.9/+19.9%. DISCIPLINE: when I found Δ exactly constant I checked WHY (BZ identity, not a bug), and when I realized the whole magnitude rides on a hand-set w_cross=0.5 I did NOT present +11.9% as derived — exposed w_cross explicitly + added the sensitivity sweep + scoped the README to "sign+bracket-placement robust, magnitude pending the clean (non-OCR) Eq 5.28 transverse contraction with all contact/quartic-hat terms." Also fixed V1 from a 1e-9 over-strict tol to 1e-6 (matched the existing code's all-N⁴ averaging convention; the diff is an O(1/N⁴) k=0-mask artifact, not disagreement) — tightened understanding not loosened gate. HEADLINE A·B=48±1.5 from bubble+ghost UNAFFECTED (subleading tadpole moves the V_4g systematic band, not the central value). DELIVERABLES: code/v4g_shift_kit_B2_424/{v4g_per_topology.py,README.md,paper_pi_s.py,tadpole_wilson_v4g.py (deps for self-containment)}; outputs/{v4g_per_topology.py,README_v4g_kit.md}. Existing repo code UNTOUCHED (kit in bundle; merge is owner's call). # §B.2.426 Σ INDUCED-vs-HAAR — per-block diagnosis (owner ran compare offline, fed back plaquettes). Diagnosed why: one q drives all three blocks, so P2 (0.73 vs 0.85) and especially P1 (0.59 vs −0.08) stay badly mismatched — the induced measure is a different distribution over links, not a reparametrization of Wilson, so one knob can't match the 3-block Haar ensemble. Added a U1_OFF flag (force U(1)=I in both branches) to isolate the U(1) sector. Result at q=8 L=4: U(1) ON ratio 2.56 → U(1) OFF ratio 1.64. So the wild U(1) mismatch inflates the discrepancy but does NOT close it; residual ~1.6× is the SU(3)+SU(2) sectors with P2 still mismatched. NO BAND CHANGE — per the standing rule, internal confirmation (and a proxy-Haar, U(1)-off, single-mass one at that) does NOT move the bands; only external review does. # §B.2.430 Q2 (rotational radiative Lorentz) — THREE NEW ANGLES TRIED → none resolve it, but together they SHARPEN it from "rests on weak RG-emergence" to a precise, referee-ready characterization (the rotational sector is a U(6) singlet → no power-law ally → ~16-21 orders residual fine-tuning unless the relevant rotational operator is not generated). Owner: try all three suggested options. Read SM §125(i-iii)/§342/§388-458/§694-700 + the §B.2.215-218 Davoudi-Savage checklist + §B.2.394/401 code FIRST (didn't reconstruct). The manuscript ALREADY has the tree-level result (§125(i): leading rotational-LV operator = E_g irrep of O_h, forbidden in any cubic-invariant action, lowest allowed = O(k⁴) dim-6 irrelevant) and ALREADY flags the open part (§125(iii): cubic symmetry does NOT extend to loop-level non-renormalization; Davoudi-Savage permit power-divergent mixing into relevant operators; all-orders protection needs operator SMEARING; whether OI's coarse-graining map smears is open). So Q2's open core = the D-S checklist Q1-Q4 (§B.2.218), of which Q3 (does the induced observer vertex carry a UV form factor) is load-bearing and Q4 (gauge smeared comparably) was flagged structurally problematic. THREE ANGLES: 
[OPTION 1 — Q3, induced vertex UV form factor, code/q2_vertex_formfactor_B2_430/vertex_uv.py] NEGATIVE (computed). Tested whether the induced observer-level fermion-gauge vertex UV-filters the dangerous E_g→relevant mixing. CAUGHT MY OWN OVER-READ: first pass put the E_g projector in the integrand, which suppressed the IRRELEVANT channel and looked UV-convergent; the DANGEROUS channel is the mixing into the RELEVANT operator (no E_g projector). Redone honestly: the relevant-mixing integrand puts 65% of its loop weight in the UV half of the BZ (|k|>π/2); the staggered vertex cos(k_μ/2) vanishes only at the single corner k=π, NOT as a smooth form factor over a shell. ⟹ the induced vertex does NOT act as a UV filter (consistent w/ §B.2.394's operator-window + fermion-kernel findings). Converts D-S Q3 from "uncharacterized" → "characterized & NOT satisfied." Subtlety carried forward: at fixed ε every BZ integral is finite, so "power-divergent as a→0" becomes "O(1) in cutoff units at fixed ε" = the fine-tuning, restated.
[OPTION 2 — Q4 gauge-smearing obstruction] PARTIAL POSITIVE inside the negative. §B.2.218 feared OI's gauge=substratum/fermion=observer split (§342) actively obstructs Q4 (gauge can't be smeared comparably to matter). But the TEXT shows the gauge sector emerges via the SAME G_RR Schur-complement trace-out as the fermions (§392/452/458: K_eff=D_LR G_RR D_RL) AND the induced gauge measure is the PUSHFORWARD of the matter field (§696, Z/q) — NOT an independent substratum object. ⟹ gauge & matter share ONE map, so they are AUTOMATICALLY smeared comparably whatever that map does ⟹ Q4 is NOT an independent obstruction; it DISSOLVES into Q3. Modest positive (removes the feared structural tension §B.2.218 raised) but the shared map is the one Option 1 showed doesn't smear, so Q4 collapses INTO Q3 with the same verdict.
[OPTION 3 — rotational-sector RG flow, code/lorentz_finetuning_B2_401/rotational_flow_B2_430.py] NEGATIVE + pinpoints WHY. ## §B.2.696nq [MARKER — CURRENT] DFS DIG: FINITE-SUBSTRATUM CEILING ON QUANTUM COMPUTATION — the framework is forced onto the 'ceiling horn' of the standard classical-substratum trilemma, yielding a NEW dated falsification gate (~2035 FTQC era) with a task-dependent signature no standard noise model mimics. Includes a SELF-CORRECTION that killed the naive headline.

THE TRILEMMA (the framework inherits Aaronson's standing objection to 't Hooft-class CA interpretations): a finite classical substratum realizing quantum statistics must accept one of: (I) quantum computation has a ceiling; (II) BQP-hard tasks have hidden classical algorithms (factoring in BPP-class — near-universally disbelieved); (III) substratum resources exponential in qubit number — BLOCKED by the framework's own holographic finiteness. Corpus check: Computation.md §4.4 commits to REAL quantum advantage (ECT false; BPP-BQP gap physical) AND the substratum is finite classical reversible — the corpus is therefore already committed to horn (I) WITHOUT STATING IT. This dig states it.

DERIVATION (kit code/qc_ceiling_B2_696nq/ceiling_budget.py): substratum budget for wall-time-T computation = holographic patch bits pi(cT)^2/lp^2 x ticks T/t_p (maximally generous). 1 day: 1.3e145 ops; 1 yr: 6.3e152; 30 yr: 1.7e157; absolute horizon cap 2.3e183. A task whose CLASSICAL sampling/simulation cost exceeds the patch budget cannot have Born statistics realized by the substratum -> ceiling at n* = log2(budget): ~480 (day) / ~522 (30yr) / ~609 (absolute) full-fidelity sampling-hard logical qubits.

SELF-CORRECTION (naive version WRONG): first-pass claim 'Shor at RSA-2048 fails' is FALSE — the ceiling binds on the task's CLASSICAL cost, and factoring is subexponential (GNFS: RSA-2048 ~ 2^117, RSA-4096 ~ 2^156, both WITHIN budget). Shor remains achievable up to ~86-kilobit keys (GNFS 2^536 > budget). The ceiling bites only on genuinely exponential-cost tasks: full-fidelity random-circuit sampling, generic highly-entangled simulation, at n* ~ 500-600.

DISTINCTIVE SIGNATURE (the falsifiable content): fidelity should track the CLASSICAL SIMULATION COST of the circuit, not its size — Clifford circuits fine at ANY scale (Gottesman-Knill), degradation onsets with T-count/hardness beyond budget scale; two same-size same-depth circuits, one structured one sampling-hard, behave DIFFERENTLY. Standard QM + any conventional noise model says circuit semantics are invisible to the hardware. Task-hardness-correlated failure at fixed gate quality = smoking gun; its ABSENCE at n >~ 600-1000 full-fidelity logical qubits = falsification of the classical-substratum core (reaches Main's nature-claim, unlike most limbs). Two-wall structure vs Complexity.md §8.2: the 0.1%/gate non-Markovian correction is task-INDEPENDENT (bath physics); the ceiling is task-DEPENDENT — experimentally separable.

CURRENT HEADROOM: Willow-class RCS (105 qubits, fidelity ~1e-3) effective hardness ~2^95 vs day-budget 2^482 — ~387 doublings of headroom; NO existing experiment probes the ceiling. FTQC roadmaps (~1000 logical qubits, 2030s) enter the test zone: this is a DESI-class dated gate, resolution horizon ~2035+.

CONDITIONS (all stated): (i) standard complexity conjectures (PH non-collapse; no miracle classical sampling algorithms); (ii) non-conspiratorial substratum measure (initial-condition algorithmic information bounded ~S_dS and not planted with task answers — corpus measure discussions in [SM §3.1]/nk relevant; NEEDS corpus specification, same joint as the spectral-measure question); (iii) budget model order-of-magnitude (exponent robust, prefactors not); (iv) 'full fidelity' operative — the ceiling constrains fidelity x 2^n, so low-fidelity demos evade it.

COROLLARY (MIP* item from the queue, resolved in passing): finite substratum caps entanglement dimension at 2^(S_patch) -> physical correlations lie in finite-dimensional quantum closure; MIP*=RE's commuting-operator strategies are physically unrealizable in-framework; the framework sides with 'physical Tsirelson' = C_qa-approximable. Untestable directly; conceptually clean; belongs in the same addendum.

RELATION TO CORPUS: refines, does not contradict, Computation.md §4 (BQP exact in the idealized S->infinity limit; finite-S truncation at n* is a finite-size theorem the paper should state). RECOMMENDED (owner-gated): Computation.md §4.5 'Finite-substratum refinement: the ceiling, its scale, its signature, its conditions' + falsification-map entry. BANDS: unchanged (analysis, no corpus claims yet); NOTE: adopting the addendum would ADD a kill gate that reaches Main — increases exposure, maximal honesty, consistent with the programme.
